note.text:
# t19_jar_drawer: notes for a fresh S2 agent (from pilot s2_t19, 2 probe episodes: FAIL then PASS)

Instruction: "Put the cream jar in the drawer and close it."

## What the scene looks like
- [seen] A small wooden one-drawer cabinet stands on the table with its drawer pulled OPEN toward the robot's right-hand side (world -y). The jar lies on a white cloth just beyond the open drawer front, on the same side. `close` and `hero` show jar, drawer and inside of the drawer best; `top` gives the layout; `wrist_right` was useless (blocked by the hand).
- [seen] `locate_objects` (with DEX_EYES_SOCKET=default): cabinet+drawer is the LARGEST object (object 0), one merged box, elongated along the slide. Its "mask part" entries split it: one part is the whole thing, one part is the cabinet body only, one small part is a piece of the drawer front. The difference between the merged box's end and the body part's end on the open side is how far the drawer is open.
- [seen] Jar and cloth are merged into one object by depth; the "mask part 2/2" entry of it (roughly square footprint a bit over 7 cm, about 5 cm high) is the jar. Take that part as the grasp target, not the merged box (that is jar+cloth).
- [seen] Class names are meaningless here (mug/cone/hammer...). Choose by size and position.

## What the task turned out to require (from the verdict after close)
- [seen] Jar resting inside the drawer, on its floor, at rest, no hand on it; drawer shut essentially FULLY (a visible 1-4 cm gap fails; it must be pushed to its stop); and the jar must have been genuinely carried by one hand for a moment (so pushing/sweeping it in would presumably not count - guess).
- [seen] The tick budget is tight (30 s). The passing episode used nearly all of it. Do not waste ticks: no go_home at the end (it cost over 400 ticks with latency in episode 0), combine perception+motion in a step, keep 300 ticks for settling.

## Sequence that passed (episode 1)
1. [seen] `grasp_scripted(view, jar_part, lift_m=0.14)` with defaults (approach from above, cup -> close). It REPORTS `capture_missed` ("target still seen where it was") both times, but the jar WAS in the hand: look at `close_rgb` - cloth empty = held. Do not retry. ~390 ticks.
2. [seen] Because the skill said "missed", the session does not believe anything is held: call `estimate_in_hand(view)` (it found the jar, source depth) and then `transport(view, Pose(point over the middle of the open part of the drawer, at rim height), hover_m=0.05)`. The point: x of the cabinet, y midway between the drawer's open end and the body's near end (a bit toward the body), z = top of the cabinet.
3. [seen] Let go with a plain dwell: `plan_motion(obs, [MotionSegment('dwell', duration_ticks=45, hand=HandCommand('open', ramp_ticks=20))])` + `execute_plan`. The jar dropped a few cm into the drawer and came to rest inside; both episodes satisfied the jar terms. `place_release` was not needed.
4. [seen] Closing the drawer: the `push` skill does NOT work here (see below). What worked is an own `plan_motion` of four segments, executed with `execute_plan`:
   free move (hand still open) to a palm-down pose (yaw 0) beside the drawer front on its outer side, about 10 cm above the working height; a dwell that makes a `fist` (ramp 25, 45 ticks); a linear descent to working height (palm origin a few cm above the cabinet top so that the fist/flange stay above the cloth but overlap the top of the drawer front); a linear segment along the slide direction toward the cabinet with `contact_links=('fingers',), exclude=<merged cabinet object>.point_cloud`.
   The side of the fist pushes the drawer front. ~210-260 ticks.
5. [seen] How far to push: in episode 0 the palm stopped about 6.5 cm short of the body's near end and the drawer stayed ~4 cm open -> FAIL. In episode 1 the goal was put 5 cm further (about 1.5 cm short of the body's near end): the palm stalled ~1 cm before its goal (the drawer hit its stop) and the drawer was fully shut -> PASS. So aim to slightly over-push; the stall is harmless at this size.
6. [seen] `retreat(view, distance_m=0.15)` then the open dwell, then close.

## What failed and why
- [seen] `push(view, cabinet_object, to_xy=..., max_stroke_m=...)`: `planning_failed / path_scene_collision` in the descent (finger 5 mm from the scene): the fist must go to 1 cm above the table and the cloth lies exactly where the fist has to come down. With the small drawer-front mask part as target (further from the cloth): `ik_unreachable`, joint 1 at limit, at the same low height.
- [seen] `guarded_press(view, Pose on the drawer front, direction=(0,1,0), max_travel_m=0.15)`: `ik_unreachable` (155 degrees off): the right arm cannot point the index finger along the closing direction here.
- [seen] `solve_ik` for the fist pose with the hand still open says `goal_scene_collision` (open thumb/fingers hang into the scene); the same pose is fine once the plan makes the fist first, higher up. A fist commanded right after dropping the jar (hand low over the drawer) is refused `start_scene_collision`: rise first, then fist.

## Guesses, not tested
- [guess] `acquire` (policy grasp) was not tried; no clip options were given. The scripted grasp sufficed.
- [guess] The scene was identical in both episodes (same perceived positions); it may not be in a counted series - perceive every time.
- [guess] A guard on the last linear segment (MotionSegment has a `guard` field) would make the over-push gentler; not tried.

note.text:
# t41_power_strip: notes for a fresh S2 agent

Instruction: "Switch on the power strip; the desk lamp should light."
From 3 development episodes (series probe, agent s2_t41, 2026-11-24): 1 FAIL, then 2 PASS.
[seen] = observed in an episode; [guess] = my inference.

## What the task turned out to require
- [seen] One press on the red pad at one end of the strip. The pad is a TOGGLE: a second press switches it off again
  (episode 0: two presses, switch ended off). Press, look at the lamp, and stop as soon as it is lit.
- [seen] The strip must stay where it lay (position and orientation), be at rest, and no hand part may touch it at the
  end. The strip is a free, light body: a press that goes too deep shoves it, and that alone fails the episode.
- [seen] The lamp lighting is visible in every colour picture (bulb glows, whole scene brightens): use it as the check.
  `guarded_press` itself returns `passed: null` / `stopped_on_guard: false` in every press here, whether it toggled or not.
- [guess] The lamp's plug staying in the strip is not a term of the rule, but a shove pulls it out, and that goes with a
  moved strip anyway.

## Seeing it
- [seen] `top` shows the strip from straight above with the red pad clearly; `close` and `hero` show the strip from the
  side and the lamp bulb. `wrist_right` is useless at home (black).
- [seen] `locate_objects` does NOT give the switch. The strip comes back merged with its cables as one long flat object
  (class named like a hammer, yaw set, top_z = the top of the plug, not of the strip's face). The lamp is not returned
  as an object at all; the largest object is the stationery at the far side with two 'mask part' entries.
- [seen] To aim at the pad: find the pad's centre pixel in `top_rgb.jpg` (zoom the crop), and convert it with the top
  camera's calibration, which the fragment can read: `view.cameras['top'].intrinsics` and `.camera_pose.position`. The
  top camera looks straight down; image right is world +y and image down is world +x:
  `x = cam_x + (v - cv) * (cam_z - z) / f`, `y = cam_y + (u - cu) * (cam_z - z) / f`. For z I took the strip object's
  `top_z` minus about 1 cm (the plug stands above the face). The fingertip landed in the middle of the pad (checked in
  the `close`/`top` pictures with `retract=False`).

## Acting
- [seen] WORKED twice: `guarded_press(view, Pose(switch_xyz, palm_down_pose(switch_xyz).quaternion_wxyz, 'world'),
  max_travel_m=0.01, speed_m_s=0.03)` then `go_home(view)` then close. The strip moved well under the allowed distance.
- [seen] FAILED: the same press with `max_travel_m=0.02` at the default speed. It toggled the switch but pushed the
  strip sideways and turned it, and pulled the lamp's plug out. The guard never stops on this light object, so
  the finger always goes the full `max_travel_m`: depth is yours to choose, the guard will not save you.
- [seen] TOO SHALLOW: `max_travel_m=0.005` did not toggle (lamp stayed dark, strip unmoved); a following press at 0.01
  did. So start shallow, look, and deepen in small steps; never repeat a press that already lit the lamp.
- [seen] Ticks: one press costs about 230 to 430 ticks (rows plus latency charged while the planner thinks, up to 150),
  go_home about 130 to 150. The budget allows about three presses plus the retreat and the 300 settle ticks.
- [seen] The right arm reaches the pad with the default press orientation; no IK trouble.
